evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: So, of course, we talked to a lot of customers everyday. Some of their concerns are damages to their items or movers not coming on time or this, any of your concerns as well?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised on-time concern; Joanna responded 'I understand. Okay, no worries. Of course if we set up a date for you, we can definitely, we rest assured that you will, will be there' — acknowledged but no follow-up probe or 'tell me more' to deepen.
evidence_quotes.value_days: So there's a price difference if we're doing it from Sunday to Thursday, usually it is a difference of about $14 per hour, $12 to $14 per hour around that. Okay, but yeah, I'll put you on a Saturday so if you adjust it will just go lower as well. — saving stated as hourly rate, not total dollar figure; no flexibility ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Call ended with 'Yes sir, I can email it. Yes sir, I do. Yes sir, thank you so much Bryan no problem. I'll send you an email after our call okay with this information.' — no rate lock, no explicit ask for the business, customer did not book.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details across special items, addresses, property type, floors, parking, walking distances, and the storage stop, establishing a clear picture for the estimate.
coaching_note: Step 2: when the customer named his on-time concern, probe deeper with 'Tell me more about that' instead of jumping to reassurance; Step 5: state Value Days savings as a total dollar amount (e.g., '$168 cheaper') not an hourly difference, and ask if he'd consider shifting dates; Step 7: deliver rate lock and no-deposit commitment, then ask directly 'Would you like our help with your move?' before routing to email.
